The merger of two major streaming platforms, HBO Max and Paramount+, may ultimately fall through.

After Netflix dropped out of the bidding war for Warner Bros. Discovery in March this year, the merger plan was announced. However, a federal judge has now issued a temporary injunction blocking the deal from going through — at least for now……

The original merger plan

Under the agreement, Paramount would acquire Warner Bros. Discovery and combine its streaming platforms HBO Max and Paramount+ into a single service.

Temporary injunction

Viewers are not keen on the plan, fearing it would reduce competition and drive up prices. A coalition of attorneys general from 12 states shares the same view and has applied to a federal court for a temporary injunction. According to NBC News, the injunction has been granted.

The injunction is valid for 14 days, pending arguments from both sides before a ruling is made. Even if Paramount ultimately wins, the merger will still need to be reviewed by the European Union and the UK government. The Writers Guild of America has also filed an antitrust lawsuit, alleging the merger would lead to layoffs and pay cuts.
